purpose: Test whether a receptor-grounded sensory front end can represent target odor identity and direction under variable wind, concentration, distractors, and mixtures without using source coordinates or navigation performance for model selection.

world.odor_channels: vector-valued; one physical concentration field per chemical component

controller_receives: body heading / proprioceptive heading representation when explicitly allowed by downstream protocol

data_selection_rule: Choose benchmark odorants by preregistered response-data coverage and receptor diversity only, before behavior or intact-vs-rewire results are observed. Do not choose odorants because the intact connectome performs well on them.
primary_direction_metrics: circular goal-direction error when target evidence is present
selection_prohibitions: no navigation score during sensory-model selection
no target label as a neural input
no post-hoc odorant selection by intact performance
no post-hoc removal of difficult mixtures
claim_boundary: Passing E003b would qualify a receptor-grounded sensory benchmark front end under the tested mixture/world assumptions. It would not establish that MaleCNS physiology implements the chosen peripheral model, that a closed-loop connectome navigates, or that intact wiring outperforms rewires.
